k3_acceptance_analysis.interpretation: K=3 is not failing uniformly. The first draft token is accepted at roughly K=1 quality, but the second and third speculative positions collapse. This points to multi-step distribution drift/exposure bias in math CoT decoding: once a draft prefix diverges even slightly from the target model trajectory, deeper speculative tokens are much less likely to match exact verifier tokens.
k3_acceptance_analysis.operational_decision: Treat K=1 as the current production-quality setting for NeMo-RL. K=2/K=3 should only be enabled behind adaptive depth or long-tail gating if per-position acceptance improves.

adaptive_gate_implementation.scope: Taming Long Tail/ReSpec-style adaptive activation and draft-depth selection for NeMo-RL/vLLM SpecDec
adaptive_gate_implementation.current_behavior: The vLLM scheduler lookahead gate starts from static request/token thresholds, measures local SpecDec enabled ratios over rolling windows, then tightens or loosens request/token thresholds toward a target enabled ratio. The scheduler request pressure now uses active requests, max(len(self.running), scheduled_requests), instead of scheduled_requests alone, so long-tail activation follows the actual active batch. The model runner now skips draft proposal only when its request/token threshold state says disabled; it no longer treats an empty scheduled_spec_decode_tokens map as a disable signal, because that can deadlock the first EAGLE draft. Adaptive mode fails fast unless at least one positive static or initial request/token threshold is configured, preventing accidental global SpecDec. ReSpec-style dynamic depth can cap the scheduler lookahead by active-batch regime, for example K=3 when active requests <=4, K=2 when active requests <=32, and K=1 otherwise. Existing patched vLLM worker environments are upgraded in place for the active-batch scheduler marker, dynamic-depth marker, and runner threshold-disabled/deadlock-fix markers instead of failing on marker drift.
adaptive_gate_implementation.metrics_visibility: NeMo-RL exposes structured spec_decode_gate metrics in addition to vLLM acceptance counters: scheduler/runner checked, enabled, disabled, enabled_ratio, last scheduled request count, last active request count, last token count, thresholds, adaptive threshold state, and dynamic draft-depth state including dynamic_last_selected_tokens. The sync worker already returned these metrics; the async worker returns the same spec_decode_gate payload and resets the gate baseline in clear_vllm_logger_metrics. A post-review fix now also emits spec_decode_gate/metrics_available=0 when SpecDec is enabled but no gate object is reachable, so missing gate metrics are explicit rather than silently absent.
adaptive_gate_implementation.default_fast_eval_plan: Qwen3-30B-A3B K=1, MAX_STEPS=8. Primary token-pressure active-batch run uses request threshold 0, token threshold 2048, adaptive target 0.75. Follow-up long-tail request-gate runs use req32+tok2048 and req64+tok2048 with adaptive target 0.50. ReSpec-style dynamic-depth run uses max K=3, req64+tok2048, active-request caps <=4 -> K3, <=32 -> K2, and larger active batches -> K1.
